fr: Il est une heure.
en: It's one o'clock.
ipa: il ɛ ynœʁ
notes: Liaison links "une" and "heure" so you hear one linked syllable; don't write an extra word between them.

fr: Il est deux heures juste.
en: It's exactly two o'clock.
ipa: il ɛ dø.zœʁ ʒyst
notes: The x in "deux" is silent alone but liaises as a z sound before "heures".

fr: Il est trois heures et quart.
en: It's a quarter past three.
ipa: il ɛ tʁwa.zœʁ e kaʁ
notes: "Et" never triggers liaison, so "quart" starts on its own consonant sound after a short pause.

fr: Il est quatre heures dix.
en: It's four ten.
ipa: il ɛ katʁ œʁ dis
notes: The final e in "quatre" is always silent, don't add an extra syllable when writing it.

fr: Il est cinq heures moins dix.
en: It's ten to five.
ipa: il ɛ sɛ̃.kœʁ mwɛ̃ dis
notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound, not a separate n consonant like in English.

fr: Il est six heures moins le quart.
en: It's a quarter to six.
ipa: il ɛ si.zœʁ mwɛ̃ lə kaʁ
notes: The x in "six" turns into a z sound before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Il est sept heures du matin.
en: It's seven in the morning.
ipa: il ɛ sɛ.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The p in "sept" is always silent, and the final t liaises into the next word.

fr: Il est huit heures du soir.
en: It's eight in the evening.
ipa: il ɛ ɥi.tœʁ dy swaʁ
notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but is pronounced here through liaison.

fr: Il est neuf heures pile.
en: It's nine o'clock sharp.
ipa: il ɛ nœ.vœʁ pil
notes: "Neuf" is an exception where the final f sound changes to v before heures.

fr: Il est dix heures et demie.
en: It's half past ten.
ipa: il ɛ di.zœʁ e də.mi
notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Il est onze heures moins cinq.
en: It's five to eleven.
ipa: il ɛ ɔ̃.zœʁ mwɛ̃ sɛ̃k
notes: "Onze" is built on a single nasal vowel sound, not two separate syllables.

fr: Il est midi et demi.
en: It's half past noon.
ipa: il ɛ mi.di e də.mi
notes: "Demi" agrees with the masculine "midi" so it keeps no final e, unlike "heure et demie".

fr: Il est minuit et demi.
en: It's half past midnight.
ipa: il ɛ mi.nɥi e də.mi
notes: "Demi" stays masculine here because it follows "minuit", not "heure".

fr: Le cours commence à midi.
en: The class starts at noon.
ipa: lə kuʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s a mi.di
notes: "À" (preposition, with accent) sounds like "a" (verb avoir) but they are spelled differently.

fr: Elle a vingt ans.
en: She is twenty years old.
ipa: ɛl a vɛ̃.tɑ̃
notes: The final t in "vingt" is silent alone but is pronounced here before "ans".

fr: J'ai quinze ans.
en: I am fifteen years old.
ipa: ʒe kɛ̃z ɑ̃
notes: "Quinze" and "ans" use two different nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling either one.

fr: Il a trente ans.
en: He is thirty years old.
ipa: il a tʁɑ̃t ɑ̃
notes: The "en" in "trente" and the "an" in "ans" sound identical though they are spelled differently.

fr: Nous avons rendez-vous à dix heures.
en: We have an appointment at ten o'clock.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.de.vu a di.zœʁ
notes: The x of "dix" liaises to a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi.
en: Today is Monday.
ipa: o.ʒuʁ.dɥi sɛ lœ̃.di
notes: "C'est" elides "ce" before a vowel, never write it as two separate words "ce est".

fr: Demain, c'est mardi.
en: Tomorrow is Tuesday.
ipa: də.mɛ̃ sɛ maʁ.di
notes: The last syllable of "demain" is a single nasal vowel, with no separate n sound.

fr: Hier, c'était dimanche.
en: Yesterday was Sunday.
ipa: jɛʁ se.tɛ di.mɑ̃ʃ
notes: "Dimanche" ends in a nasal vowel followed by "che", don't add a silent n before the ch.

fr: La classe dure une heure.
en: The class lasts one hour.
ipa: la klas dyʁ y.nœʁ
notes: "Une" and "heure" link into one sound, don't write "une" as if it stood alone.

fr: Le film commence à vingt heures.
en: The movie starts at eight PM.
ipa: lə film kɔ.mɑ̃s a vɛ̃.tœʁ
notes: The silent t of "vingt" reappears here because "heures" starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Le magasin ferme à dix-neuf heures.
en: The store closes at seven PM.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ fɛʁm a diz.nœ.vœʁ
notes: "Neuf" changes its final sound from f to v before "heures".

fr: Le bus arrive à sept heures dix.
en: The bus arrives at 7:10.
ipa: lə bys a.ʁiv a sɛ.tœʁ dis
notes: The p in "sept" is always silent, in every position, not just here.

fr: Le train part à seize heures.
en: The train leaves at four PM.
ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ paʁ a sɛ.zœʁ
notes: The final e in "seize" is silent, the word is pronounced with just one syllable ending in z.

fr: Le cours dure quarante minutes.
en: The class lasts forty minutes.
ipa: lə kuʁ dyʁ ka.ʁɑ̃t mi.nyt
notes: The "an" sound in "quarante" is a nasal vowel, don't pronounce the r and n separately.

fr: Elle arrive à midi trente.
en: She arrives at 12:30.
ipa: ɛl a.ʁiv a mi.di tʁɑ̃t
notes: "Trente" carries a nasal vowel in its first syllable, spelled en but sounding like an.

fr: Nous partons dans dix minutes.
en: We are leaving in ten minutes.
ipa: nu paʁ.tɔ̃ dɑ̃ di mi.nyt
notes: Unlike in "dix heures", the x of "dix" stays silent here because "minutes" starts with a consonant.

fr: Le magasin ouvre à huit heures et demie.
en: The store opens at half past eight.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ u.vʁ a ɥi.tœʁ e də.mi
notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before "heures".

fr: Il est presque midi.
en: It's almost noon.
ipa: il ɛ pʁɛsk mi.di
notes: "Est" (is) sounds close to "et" (and) but they are never interchangeable in writing.

fr: Le rendez-vous est à quatorze heures.
en: The appointment is at two PM.
ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu ɛ.t‿a ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ
notes: The final t of "est" is silent alone but is pronounced here before the vowel of "à".

fr: La réunion commence à seize heures trente.
en: The meeting starts at 4:30 PM.
ipa: la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s a sɛ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
notes: "Réunion" and "trente" both contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

fr: Il travaille de neuf heures à dix-sept heures.
en: He works from nine to five.
ipa: il tʁa.vaj də nœ.vœʁ a diz.sɛ.tœʁ
notes: "Neuf" again shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Le cours de français dure deux heures.
en: The French class lasts two hours.
ipa: lə kuʁ də fʁɑ̃.sɛ dyʁ dø.zœʁ
notes: The x of "deux" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Mon frère a dix-huit ans.
en: My brother is eighteen years old.
ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a di.zɥi.tɑ̃
notes: The normally silent t of "huit" is pronounced here because it liaises with "ans".

fr: Ma sœur a seize ans.
en: My sister is sixteen years old.
ipa: ma sœʁ a sɛ.zɑ̃
notes: "Ans" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it when transcribing by ear.

fr: Nous mangeons à midi juste.
en: We eat lunch right at noon.
ipa: nu mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ a mi.di ʒyst
notes: "Mangeons" keeps an extra e to preserve the soft j sound before the ending "ons".

fr: Le magasin est fermé le dimanche.
en: The store is closed on Sundays.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɛ fɛʁ.me lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
notes: "Fermé" agrees with the masculine "magasin", so it takes no extra silent e.

fr: La bibliothèque ouvre à neuf heures et demie.
en: The library opens at half past nine.
ipa: la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk u.vʁ a nœ.vœʁ e də.mi
notes: "Neuf" shifts to a v sound before the vowel of "heures" once again.

fr: Il est exactement cinq heures.
en: It's exactly five o'clock.
ipa: il ɛ.t‿ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ sɛ̃.kœʁ
notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel that liaises smoothly into "heures".

fr: Nous sommes arrivés le premier septembre.
en: We arrived on September first.
ipa: nu sɔm.z‿a.ʁi.ve lə pʁə.mje sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
notes: Only "le premier" uses the ordinal for dates, every other day uses a plain number like le deux, le trois.

fr: Elle est née le deux mars.
en: She was born on March second.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne lə dø maʁs
notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Ils sont partis le trois avril.
en: They left on April third.
ipa: il sɔ̃ paʁ.ti lə tʁwa.z‿a.vʁil
notes: "Partis" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

fr: Nous avons réservé une table pour huit heures.
en: We booked a table for eight o'clock.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl puʁ ɥi.tœʁ
notes: "Huit" liaises to a t sound before "heures" even though that t is silent on its own.

fr: Le cours a commencé à neuf heures pile.
en: The class started at nine o'clock sharp.
ipa: lə kuʁ a kɔ.mɑ̃.se a nœ.vœʁ pil
notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Elle va arriver à dix heures demain.
en: She is going to arrive at ten o'clock tomorrow.
ipa: ɛl va a.ʁi.ve a di.zœʁ də.mɛ̃
notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Nous allons partir dans deux jours.
en: We are going to leave in two days.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ dɑ̃ dø ʒuʁ
notes: "Dans" is pronounced with a single nasal vowel, not a separate n sound.

fr: Ils ont fini leurs devoirs avant minuit.
en: They finished their homework before midnight.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ fi.ni lœʁ də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ mi.nɥi
notes: "Ont" (they have) sounds identical to "on" (one, we), context tells you which to write.

fr: On a mangé à midi et demi.
en: We ate at half past noon.
ipa: ɔ̃.n‿a mɑ̃.ʒe a mi.di e də.mi
notes: "Demi" stays masculine after "midi", it only becomes "demie" after a feminine noun like heure.

fr: Elle a eu vingt ans le mois dernier.
en: She turned twenty last month.
ipa: ɛl a y vɛ̃.tɑ̃ lə mwa dɛʁ.nje
notes: The silent t of "vingt" reappears here through liaison with "ans".

fr: Nous avons rendez-vous chez le médecin à quatorze heures.
en: We have an appointment at the doctor's at two PM.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʃe lə med.sɛ̃ a ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ
notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

fr: Le magasin a fermé à dix-neuf heures hier soir.
en: The store closed at seven PM last night.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ a fɛʁ.me a diz.nœ.vœʁ jɛʁ swaʁ
notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Je vais commencer mon nouveau travail le premier juin.
en: I am going to start my new job on June first.
ipa: ʒə vɛ kɔ.mɑ̃.se mɔ̃ nu.vo tʁa.vaj lə pʁə.mje ʒɥɛ̃
notes: Dates use the ordinal only for the first of the month, all later days use plain numbers.

fr: Nous avons déménagé le quinze octobre.
en: We moved on October fifteenth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe lə kɛ̃z ɔk.tɔbʁ
notes: "Quinze" holds a nasal vowel sound in its first syllable, not a plain i.

fr: Elle est arrivée en retard à la réunion.
en: She arrived late to the meeting.
ipa: ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
notes: "Arrivée" agrees with the feminine "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Ils vont se marier le vingt et un juin.
en: They are going to get married on June twenty-first.
ipa: il vɔ̃ sə ma.ʁje lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ ʒɥɛ̃
notes: In compound numbers like vingt et un, the t of vingt is always pronounced, unlike the usual rule that et blocks liaison.

fr: Nous sommes nés la même année.
en: We were born in the same year.
ipa: nu sɔm ne la mɛm a.ne
notes: "Nés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "nous".

fr: Le train est parti à seize heures trente.
en: The train left at 4:30 PM.
ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ ɛ paʁ.ti a sɛ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
notes: With être, the past participle "parti" agrees with the masculine singular subject "le train", no extra ending.

fr: Elle a réservé son billet pour le douze mai.
en: She booked her ticket for May twelfth.
ipa: ɛl a ʁe.zɛʁ.ve sɔ̃ bi.jɛ puʁ lə duz mɛ
notes: "Son" ends in a nasal vowel, listen closely before spelling it.

fr: Nous avons attendu le bus pendant vingt minutes.
en: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy lə bys pɑ̃.dɑ̃ vɛ̃ mi.nyt
notes: The t of "vingt" stays silent here since "minutes" starts with a consonant.

fr: Ils sont rentrés chez eux avant minuit.
en: They got home before midnight.
ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.tʁe ʃe zø a.vɑ̃ mi.nɥi
notes: "Rentrés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

fr: Le film va commencer dans dix minutes.
en: The movie is going to start in ten minutes.
ipa: lə film va kɔ.mɑ̃.se dɑ̃ di mi.nyt
notes: The x of "dix" stays silent here because "minutes" begins with a consonant.

fr: Elle a fêté son anniversaire le sept mars.
en: She celebrated her birthday on March seventh.
ipa: ɛl a fe.te sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ lə sɛt maʁs
notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "anniversaire", producing an extra n sound.

fr: Nous allons voyager la semaine prochaine.
en: We are going to travel next week.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ vwa.ja.ʒe la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn
notes: The feminine "prochaine" loses the nasal sound of "prochain" because the final e opens the vowel.

fr: Le magasin ouvre à dix heures du lundi au vendredi.
en: The store opens at ten o'clock Monday through Friday.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ u.vʁ a di.zœʁ dy lœ̃.di o vɑ̃.dʁə.di
notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Elle est partie en vacances le vingt-cinq juillet.
en: She left on vacation on July twenty-fifth.
ipa: ɛl ɛ paʁ.ti ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s lə vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k ʒɥi.jɛ
notes: "Partie" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous avons un examen le trente novembre.
en: We have an exam on November thirtieth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃.z‿œ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ lə tʁɑ̃t nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ
notes: "Novembre" carries a nasal vowel right after the v, don't skip it when spelling.

fr: Ils ont raté le train de sept heures.
en: They missed the seven o'clock train.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ ʁa.te lə tʁɛ̃ də sɛ.tœʁ
notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Elle va fêter ses dix-huit ans samedi prochain.
en: She is going to celebrate her eighteenth birthday next Saturday.
ipa: ɛl va fɛ.te se diz.ɥi.tɑ̃ sam.di pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
notes: The silent t of "huit" is pronounced here because it liaises with "ans".

fr: Nous sommes sortis vers vingt et une heures.
en: We went out around nine PM.
ipa: nu sɔm sɔʁ.ti vɛʁ vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ
notes: "Heure" is feminine, so vingt et une heures uses "une", not "un".

fr: Le professeur a donné les résultats le quatre juin.
en: The teacher gave the results on June fourth.
ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a dɔ.ne le ʁe.zyl.ta lə katʁ ʒɥɛ̃
notes: Both the final s and t of "résultats" stay silent in normal speech.

fr: Nous avons déjà réservé nos billets pour le seize décembre.
en: We have already booked our tickets for December sixteenth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ de.ʒa ʁe.zɛʁ.ve no bi.jɛ puʁ lə sɛz de.sɑ̃bʁ
notes: "Décembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the s sound, easy to under-spell.

fr: Elle a répondu au message avant dix-huit heures.
en: She replied to the message before six PM.
ipa: ɛl a ʁe.pɔ̃.dy o me.saʒ a.vɑ̃ diz.ɥi.tœʁ
notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Ils vont célébrer leur anniversaire de mariage le premier octobre.
en: They are going to celebrate their wedding anniversary on October first.
ipa: il vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ də ma.ʁjaʒ lə pʁə.mje ɔk.tɔbʁ
notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal "premier", not later dates.

fr: Nous avons commencé les cours à huit heures et quart.
en: We started classes at a quarter past eight.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.se le kuʁ a ɥi.tœʁ e kaʁ
notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Elle est née un vingt-neuf février.
en: She was born on a February twenty-ninth.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne œ̃ vɛ̃t.nœf fe.vʁje
notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Le vol va décoller à minuit trente.
en: The flight is going to take off at 12:30 AM.
ipa: lə vɔl va de.kɔ.le a mi.nɥi tʁɑ̃t
notes: "Trente" carries a nasal vowel in its first syllable, spelled en but sounding like an.

fr: Nous avons visité le musée le lendemain matin.
en: We visited the museum the next morning.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te lə my.ze lə lɑ̃d.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃
notes: "Lendemain" and "matin" both end in nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

fr: Ils sont revenus deux jours plus tard.
en: They came back two days later.
ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁə.və.ny dø ʒuʁ ply taʁ
notes: The final d in "tard" is always silent in normal speech.

fr: Elle va passer son examen le vingt-trois mai.
en: She is going to take her exam on May twenty-third.
ipa: ɛl va pa.se sɔ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ lə vɛ̃t.tʁwa mɛ
notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "examen", producing an extra n sound.

fr: Nous avons attendu jusqu'à onze heures du soir.
en: We waited until eleven at night.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy ʒys.ka ɔ̃z œʁ dy swaʁ
notes: "Onze" is built on a single nasal vowel sound, not two separate syllables.

fr: Le magasin a ouvert ses portes à dix heures pile.
en: The store opened its doors right at ten o'clock.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ a u.vɛʁ se pɔʁt a di.zœʁ pil
notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Elle a oublié le rendez-vous de quatorze heures.
en: She forgot the two o'clock appointment.
ipa: ɛl a u.bli.je lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu də ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ
notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

fr: Nous allons dîner ensemble vendredi soir.
en: We are going to have dinner together on Friday evening.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ di.ne ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ
notes: "Ensemble" and "vendredi" both open with nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling.

fr: Ils ont signé le contrat le neuf septembre.
en: They signed the contract on September ninth.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ si.ɲe lə kɔ̃.tʁa lə nœf sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
notes: The final t in "contrat" is always silent in normal speech.

fr: Elle est née à sept heures du matin.
en: She was born at seven in the morning.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne a sɛ.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Nous avons fini le projet avant la date limite.
en: We finished the project before the deadline.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ fi.ni lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ a.vɑ̃ la dat li.mit
notes: The final t in "projet" is always silent in normal speech.

fr: Le cours a été annulé le vingt-six avril.
en: The class was cancelled on April twenty-sixth.
ipa: lə kuʁ a e.te a.ny.le lə vɛ̃t.sis a.vʁil
notes: "Annulé" is spelled with a double n, a common slip when writing from dictation.

fr: Elle va commencer son nouveau poste le deux janvier.
en: She is going to start her new position on January second.
ipa: ɛl va kɔ.mɑ̃.se sɔ̃ nu.vo pɔst lə dø ʒɑ̃.vje
notes: "Janvier" opens with a nasal vowel, don't confuse it with a plain a sound.

fr: Nous sommes restés jusqu'à minuit et demi.
en: We stayed until half past midnight.
ipa: nu sɔm ʁɛs.te ʒys.ka mi.nɥi e də.mi
notes: "Restés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "nous".

fr: Ils vont arriver vers dix-sept heures trente.
en: They are going to arrive around 5:30 PM.
ipa: il vɔ̃ a.ʁi.ve vɛʁ diz.sɛ.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t
notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Elle a pris rendez-vous pour le vingt et un mars.
en: She made an appointment for March twenty-first.
ipa: ɛl a pʁi ʁɑ̃.de.vu puʁ lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ maʁs
notes: In vingt et un, the t of vingt stays pronounced even though et normally blocks liaison.

fr: Nous avons célébré son anniversaire le treize juin.
en: We celebrated her birthday on June thirteenth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ lə tʁɛz ʒɥɛ̃
notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "anniversaire", producing an extra n sound.

fr: Le musée ferme à dix-huit heures le dimanche.
en: The museum closes at six PM on Sundays.
ipa: lə my.ze fɛʁm a diz.ɥi.tœʁ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
notes: "Dimanche" ends in a nasal vowel followed by che, don't add a silent n before the ch.

fr: Elle est arrivée avec une heure de retard.
en: She arrived an hour late.
ipa: ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve a.vɛk yn œʁ də ʁə.taʁ
notes: "Arrivée" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous avons pris le petit-déjeuner à sept heures et demie.
en: We had breakfast at half past seven.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi lə pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne a sɛ.tœʁ e də.mi
notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Ils ont déménagé le premier avril.
en: They moved on April first.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe lə pʁə.mje a.vʁil
notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal "premier".

fr: Elle va se réveiller à six heures du matin.
en: She is going to wake up at six in the morning.
ipa: ɛl va sə ʁe.vɛ.je a si.zœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The x of "six" turns into a z sound before the vowel of "heures".

fr: Nous avons raté notre correspondance à onze heures.
en: We missed our connection at eleven o'clock.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁa.te nɔtʁ kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃.dɑ̃s a ɔ̃z œʁ
notes: "Correspondance" and "onze" both rely on nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling.

fr: Le bébé est né à minuit pile.
en: The baby was born right at midnight.
ipa: lə be.be ɛ ne a mi.nɥi pil
notes: "Né" stays masculine to agree with "le bébé", no extra silent e is added.

fr: Elle a terminé ses études le trente juin.
en: She finished her studies on June thirtieth.
ipa: ɛl a tɛʁ.mi.ne se.z‿e.tyd lə tʁɑ̃t ʒɥɛ̃
notes: "Trente" carries a nasal vowel spelled en but sounding like an.

fr: Nous allons nous retrouver à midi devant la gare.
en: We are going to meet up at noon in front of the station.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ nu ʁə.tʁu.ve a mi.di də.vɑ̃ la gaʁ
notes: "Devant" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it.

fr: Ils sont nés le même jour, à une heure d'intervalle.
en: They were born on the same day, an hour apart.
ipa: il sɔ̃ ne lə mɛm ʒuʁ a yn œʁ dɛ̃.tɛʁ.val
notes: "Nés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

fr: Elle a acheté son billet de train pour le dix-neuf mai.
en: She bought her train ticket for May nineteenth.
ipa: ɛl a a.ʃə.te sɔ̃ bi.jɛ də tʁɛ̃ puʁ lə diz.nœf mɛ
notes: The final t in "billet" is always silent in normal speech.

fr: Nous avons discuté jusqu'à vingt-trois heures.
en: We talked until eleven PM.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ dis.ky.te ʒys.ka vɛ̃t.tʁwa.zœʁ
notes: The x of trois liaises into a z sound right before heures.

fr: Le magasin est resté fermé pendant deux semaines.
en: The store stayed closed for two weeks.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɛ ʁɛs.te fɛʁ.me pɑ̃.dɑ̃ dø sə.mɛn
notes: "Pendant" is pronounced with a single nasal vowel repeated twice, not a separate n sound.

fr: Elle va démissionner à la fin du mois.
en: She is going to resign at the end of the month.
ipa: ɛl va de.mi.sjɔ.ne a la fɛ̃ dy mwa
notes: "Fin" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it.

fr: Nous avons eu notre premier cours le lundi vingt mars.
en: We had our first class on Monday, March twentieth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ y nɔtʁ pʁə.mje kuʁ lə lœ̃.di vɛ̃ maʁs
notes: The t of "vingt" stays silent here because "mars" begins with a consonant.

fr: Ils ont eu vingt-cinq ans le même jour.
en: They turned twenty-five on the same day.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ y vɛ̃t.sɛ̃.k‿ɑ̃ lə mɛm ʒuʁ
notes: The q of "cinq" liaises into a k sound right before "ans".

fr: Elle est partie à l'aéroport à cinq heures du matin.
en: She left for the airport at five in the morning.
ipa: ɛl ɛ paʁ.ti a la.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ a sɛ̃.kœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel sound of "aéroport".

fr: Nous avons pris nos vacances la dernière semaine d'août.
en: We took our vacation the last week of August.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi no va.kɑ̃s la dɛʁ.njɛʁ sə.mɛn dut
notes: "De" elides to "d'" before "août", where the initial vowel is pronounced.

fr: Le rendez-vous a été reporté au douze juillet.
en: The appointment was postponed to July twelfth.
ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu a e.te ʁə.pɔʁ.te o duz ʒɥi.jɛ
notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

fr: Elle a fêté ses trente ans en famille.
en: She celebrated her thirtieth birthday with family.
ipa: ɛl a fɛ.te se tʁɑ̃.tɑ̃ ɑ̃ fa.mij
notes: The t of "trente" liaises before the vowel of "ans".

fr: Nous allons fêter Noël le vingt-cinq décembre comme toujours.
en: We are going to celebrate Christmas on December twenty-fifth as always.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ fɛ.te nɔ.ɛl lə vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k de.sɑ̃bʁ kɔm tu.ʒuʁ
notes: "Décembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the s sound.

fr: Ils ont raté leur avion de dix heures et quart.
en: They missed their ten fifteen flight.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ ʁa.te lœʁ a.vjɔ̃ də di.zœʁ e kaʁ
notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Elle va rentrer chez elle vers vingt-deux heures.
en: She is going to go home around ten PM.
ipa: ɛl va ʁɑ̃.tʁe ʃe zɛl vɛʁ vɛ̃t.dø.zœʁ
notes: The x of "deux" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

fr: Nous avons cours tous les jours sauf le mercredi.
en: We have class every day except Wednesday.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ kuʁ tu le ʒuʁ sof lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di
notes: The final s of "tous" is silent here because the next word starts with a consonant.

fr: Elle a envoyé le courrier avant midi.
en: She sent the mail before noon.
ipa: ɛl a ɑ̃.vwa.je lə ku.ʁje a.vɑ̃ mi.di
notes: "Envoyé" and "avant" both open with nasal vowels.

fr: Nous sommes partis en voyage le onze juillet.
en: We left on our trip on July eleventh.
ipa: nu sɔm paʁ.ti ɑ̃ vwa.jaʒ lə ɔ̃z ʒɥi.jɛ
notes: "Onze" is built on a single nasal vowel sound, not two separate syllables.

fr: Ils vont célébrer leurs retrouvailles le trente et un décembre.
en: They are going to celebrate their reunion on December thirty-first.
ipa: il vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ ʁə.tʁu.vaj lə tʁɑ̃.t‿e œ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ
notes: The t of trente stays pronounced in this compound number despite et normally blocking liaison.

fr: Elle a pris sa retraite à soixante ans.
en: She retired at sixty years old.
ipa: ɛl a pʁi sa ʁə.tʁɛt a swa.sɑ̃.tɑ̃
notes: The final t of "soixante" liaises before the vowel of "ans".

fr: Nous avons un cours supplémentaire le mardi après-midi.
en: We have an extra class on Tuesday afternoon.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃.z‿œ̃ kuʁ sy.ple.mɑ̃.tɛʁ lə maʁ.di a.pʁɛ mi.di
notes: "Supplémentaire" carries a nasal vowel in its middle syllable.

fr: Elle est née exactement à minuit.
en: She was born exactly at midnight.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ a mi.nɥi
notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous avons quitté la maison à sept heures moins le quart.
en: We left the house at a quarter to seven.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ki.te la mɛ.zɔ̃ a sɛ.tœʁ mwɛ̃ lə kaʁ
notes: The p in sept is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of heures.

fr: Ils ont célébré leur mariage le quatorze février.
en: They celebrated their wedding on February fourteenth.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ ma.ʁjaʒ lə ka.tɔʁz fe.vʁje
notes: "Célébré" repeats the accent é three times, easy to drop one when writing quickly.

fr: Elle va avoir vingt-deux ans dans trois semaines.
en: She is going to turn twenty-two in three weeks.
ipa: ɛl va a.vwaʁ vɛ̃t.dø.z‿ɑ̃ dɑ̃ tʁwa sə.mɛn
notes: The x of deux liaises into a z sound right before ans.

fr: Nous avons noté la date du seize septembre.
en: We noted the date of September sixteenth.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ nɔ.te la dat dy sɛz sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
notes: "Septembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the p sound.

fr: Le cours particulier commence à dix-huit heures trente.
en: The private lesson starts at 6:30 PM.
ipa: lə kuʁ paʁ.ti.ky.lje kɔ.mɑ̃s a diz.ɥi.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t
notes: The t of huit is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of heures.

fr: Elle a annoncé son départ pour le vingt-huit août.
en: She announced her departure for August twenty-eighth.
ipa: ɛl a a.nɔ̃.se sɔ̃ de.paʁ puʁ lə vɛ̃t.ɥi.tut
notes: "Août" starts with a vowel sound, so huit liaises directly into it.

fr: Nous sommes allés au cinéma vers vingt et une heures.
en: We went to the movies around nine PM.
ipa: nu sɔm.z‿a.le o si.ne.ma vɛʁ vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ
notes: "Heure" is feminine, so vingt et une heures uses une, not un.

fr: Ils ont fixé la réunion au cinq mai.
en: They set the meeting for May fifth.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ fik.se la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ o sɛ̃k mɛ
notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound that is easy to under-spell.

fr: Elle va prendre sa retraite le premier janvier prochain.
en: She is going to retire next January first.
ipa: ɛl va pʁɑ̃dʁ sa ʁə.tʁɛt lə pʁə.mje ʒɑ̃.vje pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal premier.

fr: Nous avons dîné ensemble le soir de son anniversaire.
en: We had dinner together on the evening of her birthday.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ di.ne ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl lə swaʁ də sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of anniversaire, producing an extra n sound.

fr: Elle est revenue de vacances le vingt et un août.
en: She came back from vacation on August twenty-first.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ʁə.və.ny də va.kɑ̃s lə vɛ̃.t‿e u.tut
notes: "Revenue" agrees with the feminine subject elle, adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous avons acheté les billets pour le concert de neuf heures.
en: We bought the tickets for the nine o'clock concert.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.ʃə.te le bi.jɛ puʁ lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ də nœ.vœʁ
notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of heures.

fr: Ils sont restés éveillés jusqu'à deux heures du matin.
en: They stayed awake until two in the morning.
ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁɛs.te e.vɛ.je ʒys.ka dø.zœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The x of deux liaises into a z sound right before heures.

fr: Elle a signé le bail à partir du premier mars.
en: She signed the lease starting March first.
ipa: ɛl a si.ɲe lə baj a paʁ.tiʁ dy pʁə.mje maʁs
notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal premier.

fr: Nous allons nous marier le vingt-neuf juin prochain.
en: We are going to get married next June twenty-ninth.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ nu ma.ʁje lə vɛ̃t.nœf ʒɥɛ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
notes: "Prochain" ends in a nasal vowel that is easy to under-spell.

fr: Ils ont annulé le vol de treize heures.
en: They cancelled the one PM flight.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ a.ny.le lə vɔl də tʁɛ.zœʁ
notes: "Treize" already ends in a pronounced z, which links smoothly into heures.

fr: Elle va avoir un entretien le trois octobre.
en: She is going to have an interview on October third.
ipa: ɛl va a.vwaʁ œ̃.n‿ɑ̃.tʁə.tjɛ̃ lə tʁwa ɔk.tɔbʁ
notes: "Entretien" opens and closes with nasal vowels, easy to under-spell.

fr: Nous avons pris le dernier train de la soirée.
en: We took the last train of the evening.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi lə dɛʁ.nje tʁɛ̃ də la swa.ʁe
notes: "Dernier" and "train" both carry nasal vowels close together.

fr: Elle est née la même année que son frère.
en: She was born the same year as her brother.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne la mɛm a.ne kə sɔ̃ fʁɛʁ
notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject elle, adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous avons noté que le cours commence à neuf heures dix.
en: We noted that the class starts at 9:10.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ nɔ.te kə lə kuʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s a nœ.vœʁ dis
notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of heures.

fr: Ils vont partir en retraite à soixante-cinq ans.
en: They are going to retire at sixty-five.
ipa: il vɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ ʁə.tʁɛt a swa.sɑ̃t.sɛ̃.kɑ̃
notes: The q of cinq liaises into a k sound right before ans.

fr: Elle a payé le loyer avant le cinq du mois.
en: She paid the rent before the fifth of the month.
ipa: ɛl a pe.je lə lwa.je a.vɑ̃ lə sɛ̃k dy mwa
notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound that is easy to under-spell.

fr: Nous avons attendu toute la matinée sans nouvelles.
en: We waited all morning without news.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy tut la ma.ti.ne sɑ̃ nu.vɛl
notes: "Matinée" and "sans" both rely on nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

fr: Le vol a atterri à vingt-trois heures cinquante.
en: The flight landed at 11:50 PM.
ipa: lə vɔl a a.tɛ.ʁi a vɛ̃t.tʁwa.zœʁ sɛ̃.kɑ̃t
notes: The x of trois liaises into a z sound right before heures.

fr: Elle a commencé ses cours de piano à cinq ans.
en: She started her piano lessons at age five.
ipa: ɛl a kɔ.mɑ̃.se se kuʁ də pja.no a sɛ̃.kɑ̃
notes: The q of cinq liaises into a k sound right before ans.

fr: Nous allons célébrer nos dix ans de mariage le vingt avril.
en: We are going to celebrate our tenth wedding anniversary on April twentieth.
ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ se.le.bʁe no di.z‿ɑ̃ də ma.ʁjaʒ lə vɛ̃.t‿a.vʁil
notes: The x of dix liaises into a z sound right before ans.
